guide.title: Colchester, Connecticut: Rubber, Bacon Academy and a Farming Colony
guide.intro: English colonists settled Colchester in 1698 on land Mohegan Sachem Uncas had granted to Jeremy Adams in 1661, and the court approved town status in 1699, naming the settlement for Colchester in Essex, England. Pierpont Bacon's 1800 will left $35,000 to found Bacon Academy in 1803; its alumni include Stephen F. Austin, the "father of Texas," and Lyman Trumbull, co-author of the Thirteenth Amendment. Nathaniel Hayward opened the Hayward Rubber Company on Lebanon Avenue in 1847, the largest industrial establishment in the town's history at nearly a thousand employees; he developed a rubber-sulfur process in the late 1830s and assigned the rights to Charles Goodyear, who patented vulcanization in 1844 and took the credit. Aided by the Baron de Hirsch Fund, Eastern European Jewish immigrants built one of Connecticut's largest Jewish farming communities here beginning in the 1890s; by 1920, half of Colchester's population was Jewish.

sections.heading: Bacon Academy, rubber and a farming colony
sections.body: Bacon Academy, founded in 1803 under Pierpont Bacon's will, still operates as Colchester's public high school on Norwich Avenue; besides Austin and Trumbull, its alumni include U.S. Supreme Court Chief Justice Morrison R. Waite. Nathaniel Hayward's rubber works on Lebanon Avenue employed nearly a thousand people at its height; Hayward donated the land for the town green and helped found the fire department and a bank, and his name survives in Hayward Avenue, Lake Hayward and the Hayward Volunteer Fire Department. Aided by the Baron Maurice de Hirsch Fund, Eastern European Jewish immigrants established a cemetery in 1894, Congregation Ahavath Achim in 1898, synagogue buildings in 1902 and 1913, a Jewish Farmers' Cooperative Credit Union in 1912 and the Colchester Farmers Produce Company in 1916. In 2010 Colchester became the first Connecticut town, and the 36th nationally, certified as a Community Wildlife Habitat by the National Wildlife Federation.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Colchester sits roughly midway between Hartford and New London along CT Route 2, where Route 11's short expressway from Salem comes to an end; there is no passenger rail station in town, so travelers by train use Shore Line East and Amtrak at New London or Old Saybrook and finish the trip by car. Route 11, a 7.1-mile freeway from Route 82 in Salem, was meant to continue toward Waterford, but only about half the planned route was ever built and the extension was formally abandoned in October 2016 — which is why the highway simply ends onto Colchester's two-lane roads. Route 16 runs past Salmon River State Forest, and Route 149 carries an Air Line State Park Trail trailhead.

sections.heading: Trails, a working farm and where to eat
sections.body: Day Pond State Park's mill-pond trails connect to Salmon River State Forest and its 1873 Comstock Covered Bridge, jointly built by Colchester and neighboring Chatham, now East Hampton; the Air Line State Park Trail follows the route of the 1870s Air Line Railroad through town on its way toward the Hop River Trail. Zagray Farm Museum, a working antique-machinery collection, opens to the public chiefly for three annual weekend shows, and Cato Corner Farm sells its own raw-milk farmstead cheese from an on-site store. The Colchester History Museum, run by the Colchester Historical Society on Linwood Avenue, covers the town's rubber, education and Jewish farming history. For food, Harry's Place has served burgers and hot dogs since 1920, Oz'N Bones BBQ and Fornarelli's Ristorante anchor the sit-down scene, and Hop Culture Farms & Brew Co. pours from its Cato Corner Road taproom. The O'Connell House, an 1840 Greek Revival bed and breakfast on Broadway, is the only lodging verified inside town limits.

faq.question: How do I get to Colchester?
faq.answer: By car — CT Route 2 runs through town, and Route 11's short expressway from Salem ends at Route 2. There is no passenger rail station in Colchester; the nearest stations are Shore Line East and Amtrak stops at New London or Old Saybrook.

faq.question: Is there a train to Colchester?
faq.answer: No. Shore Line East runs along the shoreline through New London and Old Saybrook, well south of Colchester, and no branch line reaches town.

faq.question: What is the Comstock Covered Bridge?
faq.answer: An 1873 covered bridge over the Salmon River, jointly built by Colchester and Chatham (now East Hampton) for about $4,000. It sits within Salmon River State Forest on the East Hampton side, not at a Colchester address, and is preserved for pedestrians.

faq.question: Is there a hotel in Colchester?
faq.answer: The O'Connell House, a four-room bed and breakfast in an 1840 Greek Revival building on Broadway, is the only lodging verified inside Colchester. Book well ahead.

faq.question: What is Colchester's Jewish farming history?
faq.answer: Aided by the Baron de Hirsch Fund, Eastern European Jewish immigrants built one of Connecticut's largest Jewish farming communities here starting in the 1890s, with a cemetery, synagogue, credit union and produce cooperative; by 1920 half the town's population was Jewish. Congregation Ahavath Achim's 1913 synagogue still stands.

places.name: Day Pond State Park
places.summary: A pond the pioneering Day family dug to power an "up and down" sawmill, with stone foundations of the mill complex still visible. A roughly five-mile trail network links the park to Salmon River State Forest and reaches a series of waterfalls up to ten feet tall. Open 8 a.m. to sunset, April through Columbus Day, free.

photos.title: Day Pond State Park
photos.description: Lily pads and the stone retaining wall at Day Pond State Park's swimming beach.
photos.author: Magicpiano

places.name: Salmon River State Forest
places.summary: Nearly 7,000 acres spanning Colchester, East Haddam, East Hampton, Hebron and Marlborough, with the 6.7-mile blue-blazed Salmon River Trail and the 1873 Comstock Covered Bridge on the East Hampton side. Trout fishing, hunting, picnicking and biking on the Air Line State Park Trail are permitted. Open daily 8 a.m. to sunset, free, leashed pets.

places.name: Air Line State Park Trail
places.address: Colchester trailheads on Route 149, Bull Hill Road, River Road and Old Hartford Road, Colchester, CT 06415
places.summary: A 50-mile multi-use rail-trail on the route of the 1870s Air Line Railroad, whose white-and-gold cars gave the line its "Ghost Train" nickname. It carries a segment of the East Coast Greenway through Colchester and connects toward the Hop River Trail. Free, leashed pets welcome.

places.name: Zagray Farm Museum
places.summary: A working antique-machinery and farm-history museum run by the Quinebaug Valley Engineers Association, open chiefly for three annual weekend shows: Spring Show and GAS UP! (May 2-3, 2026), Summer Show (July 18-19, 2026) and Fall Show (October 3-4, 2026). Admission $10, ages 15 and under free.

places.name: Cato Corner Farm
places.summary: A Connecticut farmstead producer of raw-milk cheese with an on-site farm store. Open Fridays and Saturdays 10 a.m.-4 p.m., Sundays 11 a.m.-4 p.m.

places.name: Colchester History Museum
places.summary: Run by the Colchester Historical Society, with four exhibit rooms on the town's rubber industry, education history and Jewish farming community, including "Emerging from the Shadows: the Story of Colchester's School for Colored Children, 1803-1840." Free admission; call (860) 537-4230 for open days.

places.name: Harry's Place
places.summary: A seasonal roadside burger and hot-dog stand open since 1920, also serving seafood, chicken, sandwiches and ice cream. Open daily from 11 a.m., March through October. Phone (860) 537-2410.

places.name: Oz'N Bones BBQ
places.summary: Artisan barbecue — chicken, brisket and ribs — with cornbread and maple butter, plus a Saturday brunch. Open Tue-Thu 11:30 a.m.-8 p.m., Fri 11:30 a.m.-9 p.m., Sat 11 a.m.-9 p.m. with brunch 11-2, closed Sun-Mon. Phone (860) 537-3355.

places.name: Hop Culture Farms & Brew Co.
places.summary: A farm brewery taproom on Cato Corner Road. Open Thursday 4-9 p.m., Friday-Saturday 12-10 p.m., Sunday 12-6 p.m., closed Monday-Wednesday. Contact team@hopculturefarms.com.

places.name: Fornarelli's Ristorante & Bar
places.summary: Italian-style family dining across two levels, with pasta, seafood, antipasti and a full bar; a special Monday menu runs Monday 3-9 p.m. Open Tue-Wed 11:30 a.m.-9 p.m., Thu to midnight, Fri-Sat to 1 a.m., Sun 11:30 a.m.-8 p.m. Phone (860) 531-9160.

places.name: The O'Connell House
places.summary: An 1840 Greek Revival house renovated into a bed and breakfast with four guest rooms sleeping up to twelve, booked through Airbnb. The only lodging verified inside Colchester. Phone (860) 537-1925.
